title: CERT-In advisory CIAD-2026-0062: unauthorised transactions through business payment workflows, including government-linked payment providers
date_note: Date is the original issue date of CERT-In advisory CIAD-2026-0062 (20 November 2026); the advisory gives no dates for the transactions it reports.
place: New Delhi, India (agency location; victims not named)
summary: CERT-In's advisory CIAD-2026-0062 of 20 November, rated Critical, says it has received reports of unauthorised financial transactions involving organisations outside the financial sector, including service providers supporting government-linked payment workflows and vendor or partner payout platforms. It says attackers altered business records or approval relationships, then used legitimate payment processes. The advisory names no victims and gives no amounts; Reuters also says no amounts or payers were given.
plain: India's cyber agency says fraudulent payments were made by changing business records or approvals at service providers, including ones handling government-linked payments. No victims or amounts were given.
exec: India's national CERT reports payment fraud through altered records at service providers and payout platforms; no amounts or victims were disclosed.
action: CERT-In advises identifying service-provider accounts that can change payment records or approve transactions, reconciling payment instructions against independent records, and requiring independent verification for changes to payment instructions, beneficiaries and approvals.

validation.note: Primary source: CERT-In's own advisory CIAD-2026-0062 (issued 20 November 2026), read by the follow-up desk on 22 November; it confirms the Reuters account (relayed by ThePrint) and The420.in. The advisory says the transactions involve organisations outside the financial sector, so the title no longer says financial service providers. The same advisory is already on file as cert-in-ai-driven-payment-workflow-attacks-warning-2026-11 (first seen 21 November 12:38 UTC, earlier than this record), so this record is marked duplicate_of it.

review.note: Compared title, date (Friday 20 Nov), summary wording, absence of amounts and payer, single_source validation, severity 2 against ThePrint (Reuters) and The420.in; nothing added; CERT-In advisory itself not read, as the record states.
